source_text: VI. Ἀλέξανδρός δέ τις ἀγοραῖος πονηρὸς ἀνὴρ εἶπεν· Ἄκουσον ἡμῶν, Πιόνιε. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ἐπιλαβοῦ σὺ παρ᾽ ἐμοῦ ἀκούειν· ἃ γὰρ σὺ οἶδας οἶδα, ἃ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐπίσταμαι σὺ ἀγνοεῖς. Ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος ἠθέλησεν αὐτοῦ καταγελᾶν, ἐπεὶ καί φησιν εἰρωνείᾳ· Ταῦτα δὲ διὰ τί; Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ταῦτα ἵνα μὴ διερχόμενοι τὴν πόλιν ὑμῶν ὑπονοηθῶμεν ὡς μιαροφαγήσοντες προσεληλύθαμεν, καὶ ἵνα μάθητε ὅτι οὐδὲ ἐπερωτᾶσθαι ἀξιοῦμεν ἀλλὰ κρίναντες οὐκ εἰς τὸ Νεμεσεῖον ἀλλ᾽ εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ἀπερχόμεθα, καὶ ἵνα μὴ ὡς τοὺς λοιποὺς βίᾳ ἡμᾶς συναρπάσαντες ἀπαγάγητε, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ φορεῖν δεσμὰ ἐάσητε· τάχα γὰρ μετὰ δεσμῶν οὐκ εἰσαγάγετε ἡμᾶς εἰς τὰ εἰδώλεια ὑμῶν. Καὶ οὕτως ὁ Ἀλέξανδρος ἐφιμώθη. Καὶ πάλιν ἐκείνων πολλὰ παρακαλούντων αὐτὸν ἐκείνου λέγοντος· Οὕτω κεκρίκαμεν, καὶ πολλὰ ἐλέγχοντος αὐτοὺς καὶ περὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἀπαγγέλλοντος αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἀλέξανδρος εἶπεν· Τίς γὰρ χρεία ἐστί, φησίν, τῶν λόγων ὑμῶν τούτων ὁπότε οὐκ ἔξεστιν ὑμᾶς ζῆν;
pass_a_gloss: But a certain Alexander, a marketplace-lounging base man, said: Hear us, Pionius. Pionius said: Hold yourself back from hearing from me; for what you know I know, but what I understand you do not know. And Alexander wanted to mock him at him, since he also says with irony: But these things, for what reason? Pionius said: These things so that, while passing through your city, we may not be suspected that we have come as men about to eat polluted food, and so that you may learn that we do not even think it fit to be interrogated but, having decided, we are going away not to the Nemeseion but to the prison, and so that you may not, as with the rest, seize us by force and lead us away, but may leave us alone because we wear bonds; for perhaps with bonds you will not lead us into your idol-places. And in this way Alexander was muzzled. And again, while those men were earnestly urging him, while he was saying: Thus we have decided, and while he was much reproving them and reporting to them concerning the coming things, Alexander said: For what need is there, he says, of these words of yours, when it is not permitted for you to live?
pass_b_english: Then a certain Alexander, a worthless fellow loitering about the marketplace, said, Hear us, Pionius. Pionius answered, Take up hearing from me, for what you know I also know, but what I understand you do not know. Alexander wanted to laugh him down, and so he said with sneering irony, But why all this? Pionius replied, All this so that as we pass through your city we may not be suspected of having come to eat defiled food, and so that you may learn that we do not even ask to be examined but have made our decision and are going not to the shrine of Nemesis but to the prison, and so that you may not seize us by violence as you did the rest and drag us off, but may let us alone because we wear chains, for with our chains upon us you will perhaps not drag us into your idol-houses. And with that Alexander was muzzled.

And again, while the others kept pleading with him at length, he kept answering, This is our decision, and he rebuked them sharply and told them of the things to come, until Alexander said, What use, he asks, are these words of yours, when you are not permitted to live?

choices.reason: draft inverted it to holding back — ἐπιλαμβάνω takes hold, it does not hold back
the eating itself, not polluted feasts
